alignments.note: Dative pronoun; the ASV writes no case preposition.
Rule 23: article before a name with no English realization.
Name, fronted by the ASV under rule 15.
φιμόω rendered by the idiom *Hold thy peace*; rule 17's meaning-bearing complement puts the head on *peace*, no English word answering to the verb's lexeme separately.

Corrected: the imperative keeps only *come*. Rule 106 is scoped in terms to a particle **no Greek preposition stands to answer to**, and here ἐξ stands and is exactly the word *out* answers to, so rule 106 does not put the particle inside the verb's unit and rule 94 decides the prepositional pair instead.

Corrected: the two-word English preposition *out of* renders the single Greek preposition whole, headed on *out*. Rule 94 splits the pair from αὐτοῦ, the ASV writing more than one English word; rule 36 gives the preposition governing the phrase to the Greek preposition even where English idiom makes the verb phrasal, and a bare *of* is a deficient rendering of ἐκ, whose own gloss is *out of*. The competing reading — *out* to the preverb and *of* here — is what the earlier alignment took, and 1:16's `παράγων παρά` → *passing along by* is the case where it is right, παρά having its own full word *by*.

review_notes: The correction is confined to *come out of him*: rule 106's scope clause hands the particle to the expressed preposition, so ἐξ takes *out of* headed on *out* and ἔξελθε keeps a bare *come*.
Everything else stands: the article before Ἰησοῦς is `unrepresented` under rule 23, and Φιμώθητι takes the whole idiom *Hold thy peace* headed on the meaning-bearing complement.
